_comment: SD17 -- the Burrow Warrens, the Meadows' one required dungeon (MEADOWS_PROGRESSION_SPEC.md Sec3 Band 2). A COMPACT cave, not a puzzle box: five chambers, one gated side branch, aggressive Ground creatures, Rootstone in the walls, and one guardian that has to be beaten. ALL NUMBERS TUNABLE per CLAUDE.md. scripts/world/burrow_warrens.gd is the only reader.
_comment_site: `entrance.at` is world metres [x, z]; `entrance.yaw_deg` turns the cave's LOCAL +z (its depth axis) toward the rocky rise at [140,-90], so walking in walks INTO the hill. The site was measured, not guessed (a throwaway probe over data/config/terrain_playground.json's own heightfield): [70,-140] is the flattest approach of five candidates on that flank -- 8 degrees of local relief over 4m against 46-54 degrees at every candidate further up the flank, which the spawns.json header already records as unwalkable ground. Terrain along the depth axis climbs 0.3 -> 10.7 -> 20.9 -> 27.0m at 0/20/30/40m in, so the mouth chamber's roof breaks the surface as a rocky outcrop and everything past it is genuinely buried. It sits ~143m south-east of the village square, past where the deeper Meadows begins, and a short walk from the Burrowback cluster spawns.json already places at [55,-145] -- the warrens is where they come from.
_comment_floor: The cave floor is ONE level, `floor_clearance` above the terrain height at the mouth. What makes a flat floor honest here is no longer rising ground -- see `_comment_resiting`: there is no rising ground in this part of the Meadows, and the cave stands in a rock knoll of its own on the flattest ground within 60m. A flat floor is what that site supports; a descending one would put the ground surface inside the deeper rooms. `wall_thickness`, `skirt` (how far floor slabs and walls extend BELOW the floor, so nothing floats where the hillside falls away) and `rock` colours are presentation, all tunable.
_comment_ow5d_relocation: OW5D, docs/MEADOWS_MACRO_LAYOUT.md section 10.2: `site.at` moves from (70,-140) to (-420,2470). Everything else in this file (chambers, passages, lights, spawns, deposits, prize) is authored in the SITE'S OWN LOCAL frame per `_comment_site`/`_comment_floor` above and rotates/translates with `site.at`+`site.yaw_deg` automatically, so none of it needed editing. `yaw_deg` (54.5) is left UNCHANGED -- the relocation table gives only a new position, not a new approach bearing, and re-deriving it for the new site's actual hillside would need fresh ground probing (this file's own `_comment_site` explains the original 54.5 was picked from a 5-candidate probe of the OLD flank at [140,-90], which no longer describes anything at the new site). Ground truth at the new site was NOT probed by this pass (see the OW5D report) -- flagging per the macro-layout doc's own instruction that `burrow_warrens.json`'s 10m `skirt` needs ground that will accept it. `harvest.json`'s five ironwood nodes move with this site at the same offset (-490,+2610).
_comment_resiting: BAND2-63-WARRENS, 2026-08-22. `site.at` moves to (-357,2610) and `yaw_deg` to 315.0, from OW5D's (-420,2470)/54.5. The reason is not taste: at the OW5D site the cave could not be walked through. `tools/_probe_warrens_run.gd` drove the player in and wedged them solid at local z=27.5 against a collider named `Terrain`, five metres short of the passage to the den -- the guardian, the clear flag and the heartstone were all unreachable on foot, and `tests/smoke_warrens.gd` never saw it because it teleported the player into each chamber rather than walking between them. The cause is the one OW5D's own `_comment_ow5d_relocation` (below, kept) wrote down and left open: it translated a cave whose geometry had been measured against a specific steep flank at (70,-140) onto ground nobody had probed, and kept the bearing derived for the old flank. At (-420,2470) the ground rolls; it does not rise. `tools/_probe_warrens_site.gd` measures that chamber by chamber, and its modes rule out the obvious fixes in turn: another bearing does not clear it (`--scan`), no origin on a 25m grid out to 300m clears it (`--sites`, run from this site AND from the Old Quarry -- the best anywhere is 2.6m short of burying 4-6m ceilings), and making the cave DESCEND (`--plan`) buries the deep rooms but not the entrance, because the ground surface then cuts through the entry corridor and the player walks up it into the ceiling. There is no flank in this part of the Meadows. What works is `--mound`: stand the cave where the terrain never rises above its floor at all, so nothing intrudes anywhere, and let what shows above ground be a rock knoll with a hole in it -- which is what this file's own site comment always said the entrance was, and what `skirt` was built to hide the underside of (see `_comment_mound` for the outcrop that makes it read as stone rather than as a slab). The first such site, (-382,2510), cleared the footprint and failed the OTHER half nobody had checked: the driven run walked 30m from the road and stopped 25m short of the entrance, against a 50-degree bank. `--best` scores both at once -- footprint clear, the 40m in front of the mouth walkable, and the site kept near the spine -- and (-357,2610) at 315 degrees is its answer: clear by 0.43m, approach 6.9 degrees, 34m off the spine, sitting on the `warren_undertrail` loop that terrain_playground.json already runs past the warrens. The whole path now walks: road to entrance to mouth to hall to den to vault, 123m, 26s, measured. Everything sited against the old mouth moved with it: Pell's stand (trainers.json order 2001, 35m out on the approach), the five ironwood nodes (harvest.json), the warrens' own resident Burrowback cluster (spawns.json order 3) and the map region (map_landmarks.json). The chamber layout, sizes, spawns, deposits, dressing and prize are UNCHANGED -- they are authored in the site's own local frame and rotate with it, which is the property `_comment_site` describes. One dependency is NOT this lane's to close: the scatter still has a `CommonTree_3` standing in the new doorway, because a band clearing does not invalidate the bake (GATE_D_LANE_CONTRACT.md sec4). The clearing is authored (bands/band2_stone_and_root/vegetation.json order 2002, radius 30) and the walked evidence above was measured with the 93 scatter colliders inside it dropped, which is what the coordinator's single re-bake will do for real.

site._comment_clear_radius: BAND2-63-WARRENS. Matches the authored clearing in bands/band2_stone_and_root/vegetation.json (order 2002) and is applied at BUILD time by burrow_warrens.gd::_clear_the_ground_the_cave_stands_on(), because that authored clearing cannot take effect until the coordinator re-bakes (GATE_D_LANE_CONTRACT.md sec4) and until then the stale bake stands a tree in the doorway. Keep the two numbers the same: when the re-bake lands, the runtime pass has nothing left to remove and this becomes a no-op rather than a second, disagreeing opinion about where the wood stops.
site._comment_vault_door_seam: CONTENT-0828. The shut branch door was a grey slab the same value as the wall it sits in, so from the den floor it was a wall: the player fought the guardian in a room with no visible reason to be there and found the branch afterwards, if at all. `seam` is a thin emissive line down the door's own face and a warm spill on the VAULT side of it, so what the player can see across the den WHILE THE ALPHA IS STILL ALIVE is a shut way on with something lit behind it. That is the difference between a fight at the end of a corridor and a fight for what is through the door, and it is the `encounter context` lever CLAUDE.md names -- no new mesh, no new system. `open_seconds` is how long the slab takes to sink when the guardian falls; it animates ONLY on that transition, never on a returning player's build (burrow_warrens.gd::_sync_vault_door). Set `energy` to 0 to turn the whole treatment off. ALL TUNABLE.

vault_door_seam._comment_under: CONTENT-0828B. The spill above is on the VAULT side and only a player already looking at the door sees it. tools/_probe_den_door_sightline.gd measured the sightline from the stands a player is actually at -- the den doorway and a ring at engage range around the guardian -- and the shut door is on screen at one of eight: it reads on the way in and then leaves the frame for the whole fight, because the guardian is in the middle of the room and the door is on a side wall. `under_*` is a low warm pool at the foot of the slab on the DEN side, which is in frame from every facing because it lights the floor the player is standing on. Scaled off the seam's own energy so retuning one retunes both; set `under_energy_scale` to 0 to remove it.

_comment_mound: BAND2-63-WARRENS. The cave stands in ground that does not cover it (see `_comment_resiting`), so what a player sees from the road is the cave's own rock mass standing proud of the meadow -- and the first capture round showed exactly what that is without help: a grey rectangular slab, six metres tall, in a field. This is the outcrop that makes it a knoll instead. Deterministic boulders from the nature family the corridor is already scattered with (`Rock_Medium_1..3`, the same models `vegetation.json` uses), set around the perimeter and over the roof so the silhouette breaks up and the mass reads as stone in the ground rather than a building. Seeded, never random: the same rock stands in the same place every boot, which is the determinism promise the rest of the world keeps. `skip_front_m` keeps the DOORWAY clear and nothing else -- it was 9m, which left the whole front of the cave as a bare flat rectangle standing in a field, and the blind critic called it exactly that: a textured plane with straight cut edges reading as unfinished blocking geometry. At 6m the rock runs across the front too and the opening reads as a hole in a rock face. `tint` multiplies the boulders' own albedo toward the cave's rock colour, because the nature pack's rocks ship a cool mint-grey that the same critic read as 'a heap of enormous cabbages' beside this cave's warm dark stone. ALL TUNABLE.

mound._comment_skirt: The site clears 30m of scatter so nothing stands in the cave or its doorway, and the first blind round showed the cost of that honestly: a bare lawn ring around the outcrop, in a survey whose loudest criticism was already ground density. These are the site's OWN ground cover, authored rather than scattered -- broken rock and low planting banked against the outcrop where debris and shade would actually put them, thinning outward. Same nature family the corridor already uses (D24, one nature family), deterministic from the same seed, no colliders: this is dressing, and a pebble that stops a player is a bug.

_comment_chambers_heights: BAND2-63-WARRENS lowered every ceiling by 0.6-1.2m (mouth 4.2->3.6, hall 5.0->4.2, warren 4.0->3.4, den 6.0->4.8, vault 4.0->3.4). At this site most of the cave's mass stands ABOVE the meadow (see `_comment_resiting`), so every metre of ceiling is a metre of grey slab on the skyline; the first capture round showed a six-metre wall. They are still taller than the player and taller than the guardian, and the den is still the tallest room in the cave -- the shape of the place is unchanged, it is just not a tower any more. `lights[].y` moved with the two ceilings it would otherwise have poked through. TUNABLE.
_comment_chambers: Local metres: x is lateral, +z is depth into the hill; `at` is the chamber centre, `size` is [width, depth], `height` is floor-to-ceiling. Chambers connected by a passage MUST share the axis the passage runs on (the wall opener splits one wall, it does not cut diagonals). `branch: true` marks the optional deep branch -- it is not on the way to anything.
_comment_passages: `gated: true` is the one door in the cave: a rock slab across the den->vault passage that only lifts once `clear.flag` is set (see `guardian`). Deliberately NOT an item_gate.gd gate -- SB10's mechanism is a carried KEY operating the world, and nothing in the warrens hands out a key; the thing that opens this is having beaten the guardian, which is a fact about the world the flag store already remembers.
_comment_lights: Dim on purpose. OF24 shipped a carried torch and this is the place it is supposed to matter, so these are low-energy pools that shape the chambers without lighting them -- a player who walks in without a torch should be able to find the way back out and not much else. `at` is [x, z] local plus `y` above the floor.
_comment_lights_authored: CONTENT-0828. Playtest 4a's own candidate direction: 'lighting authored per space rather than inherited'. Every chamber had exactly one dim pool of roughly the same energy in roughly the same place, which lights a room evenly and therefore says nothing about it -- an even wash is the lighting equivalent of the flat wall. The dark stays dark (the cave is authored dim on purpose and OF24's torch is what reads it, see `_comment_lights`); what changes is that the two rooms the dungeon exists for now have a SHAPE. The den's own fill drops 0.6 -> 0.40 and a warmer key washes the guardian's half of the room, so the alpha stands in warm light in a room that falls off cool around it rather than being one more evenly-lit object. Round 1 of this put that key at y=3.9 with range 9.5 and the frames showed it lighting the CEILING while the guardian went to silhouette -- and taught the other half of the lesson: the guardian is a wild body with a `home` and it WANDERS, so a tight spot on its authored stand cannot track it. It is a broad wash over its half of the den instead (y 3.9 -> 3.1, range 9.5 -> 13), which is a thing a room can have and a spotlight is not. The vault keeps its warm pool and gains a low cool bounce at the door end, so the chamber reads as deep rather than as a lit box -- the heartstone's own OmniLight (burrow_warrens.gd::_build_prize) is still the brightest thing in it, which is the point. The other three chambers are unchanged. ALL TUNABLE.
_comment_interior_rock: CONTENT-0828. The owner localised the looks complaint on 2026-08-28 -- 'burrow warrens and the castle are the lame looking locations. basically everywhere we had to build an under ground or build a building' -- and this is the half of the answer that needs no owner art. The terrain, scatter and grass drew no complaint; the two ASSEMBLED spaces did, and this cave's own before-frames say why: docs/evidence/content-0828/04-vault-prize-after.png is a perfect rectangular box -- four flat walls meeting at hard 90-degree corners, a flat ceiling, a flat floor, one triplanar texture at one scale over all of it, next door to a meadow with hundreds of pieces of variety per comparable area. It does not read as unfinished because the rock texture is bad. It reads as unfinished because a cave does not have corners. So this breaks the three junctions that say 'box' and nothing else: the wall/floor line (boulders banked along the inside of each wall), the wall/ceiling line (rock in the four ceiling corners only -- the ceiling's MIDDLE stays clear on purpose, because rock over the guardian's head is the frame this pass exists to stop producing) and the flat floor (scree thinning inward from the walls). Everything sits within `edge_band_m` of a wall, so the middle of every room is untouched and a den fight keeps the arena combat_arena_bounds_at() promises it; nothing goes in a doorway; and none of it has colliders, the rule _build_site_skirt()'s own comment states -- this is dressing, and a pebble that stops a player is a bug. Same nature family as the outcrop outside and the same `mound.tint`, per D24: the stone inside the hill and the stone showing above it are the same stone. `enabled: false` turns the whole pass off. ALL TUNABLE.

interior_rock._comment_tint: Round 1 of this pass reused `mound.tint` (#c3bbab) and the frames said no: that value was tuned against the outcrop standing in DIRECT SUN, and under the cave's dim cool pools the nature pack's mint-grey came back through it -- the same green a blind critic called 'a heap of enormous cabbages' on the mound in BAND2-63 round 1, now inside the room. `_tint_rock()` multiplies albedo, so the tint has to do the whole job of turning mint into stone here rather than assisting sunlight. This is pulled hard toward the cave's own `site.rock` warmth: against the mint source it lands a warm brown-grey, which is the colour the walls three feet away already are. Interior and exterior rock are still the same models from the same family (D24); they are lit by different light and so they are tinted for it.
interior_rock._comment_material: Round 2 tinted these rocks twice and the frames said green both times. `_tint_rock()` MULTIPLIES albedo, which is the right tool outside -- it keeps each rock's own shading under strong sun and two blind rounds tuned the mound with it -- but under 0.3-1.5 energy pools the multiply does almost none of the work and what survives is the model's own mint texture. So the interior rock now wears the SAME triplanar Rock030 material the chamber walls wear (burrow_warrens.gd::_wear_the_cave_stone). Triplanar is what makes that legal on models whose UVs were authored for something else -- it projects from world space and needs no UVs, the same reason the walls use it on primitive boxes. `tint` is no longer a colour correction; it is the per-piece VARIATION, each rock taking the site's own rock colour nudged 35% toward this value so a bank along a wall is not one flat sheet of identical stone.
interior_rock._comment_caps: Round 2 capped HEIGHT and said nothing about WIDTH, and the frames showed the cost: a five-metre-wide rock sitting correctly against the den wall still reaches two and a half metres into the room, and one ended up between the camera and the guardian -- the exact failure this pass exists to replace. Both caps are metres, applied to each piece's MEASURED bounds rather than to a scale factor, because these models arrive at different sizes and a scale number means nothing across them.

_comment_interior_structure: CONTENT-0828B. The other half of the owner's 4a diagnosis, and the half `interior_rock` above deliberately did not attempt -- its own report: 'the walls themselves are still flat planes and the ceiling is still a slab between its corners. This pass changes what the room's EDGES do; it does not give the space vertical interest, level changes, or a silhouette.' The owner named a CLASS of space ('basically everywhere we had to build an under ground or build a building'), so the answer is a shared method rather than a second dressing pass on one cave: scripts/world/interior_structure.gd, which stronghold.json consumes from the same file with its own vocabulary. That file's header carries the mechanism; the short version is that a chamber built from six flat boxes has exactly two scales of incident (the room, and its props) where the meadow outside has five or six, and that missing MIDDLE scale is what makes an interior read as blockout however good its texture is. The five passes put it back: a vertical member at a repeating pitch along every wall (`bays`), a jointed horizontal band at mid-height (`course`), ceiling ribs landed on the same divisions so the structure reads as continuous (`ribs`), a jamb-and-lintel frame around every cut opening (`reveals`), and a post in each internal corner (`corners`). None of it is solid, none of it enters a doorway, and none of it reaches further into a room than interior_structure.gd's own MAX_PROJECT_M -- half the metre `combat_arena_bounds_at()` reserves from every wall, so the den fight keeps the arena it was tuned against. ALL TUNABLE; `enabled: false` turns the whole pass off.
_comment_interior_structure_cave: This cave's VOCABULARY, against the castle's. `jitter` above zero is the whole difference in code: each member takes a small lean, inset and scale variation, so the same rhythm that reads as masonry in the stronghold reads as rock ribbing here. 0.85 rather than 1.0 because past that the members stop lining up with each other and the rhythm -- which is the point of the pass -- stops reading. `bay_pitch_m` is tighter than the stronghold's (2.9 against 3.6): these chambers are 7-16m across and 3.4-4.8m tall, and a pitch tuned for a 28m hall gives a small room one member and no rhythm at all. `tints` are per-role value steps off `site.rock`; they exist because every light in this cave is a shadowless omni (`_build_lights`), so nothing here is going to model the form for us and a member the same value as the wall behind it is invisible however well it is shaped. Omit a role and burrow_warrens.gd::_structure_colour derives it.

interior_structure._comment_ragged: CONTENT-0828B round 4. `jitter` alone did not make this read as a cave: a blind critic given the ribbed build said nothing in the Warrens reads as burrowed and that it is 'built out of the same dressed ashlar as the fortress'. Fair -- a few degrees of lean on a member that still runs floor to ceiling at a regular pitch is a colonnade with a wobble. `ragged` gives each member its own height and width, so ribs DIE OUT partway up the wall the way harder stone in a cave does, and a member that stops short loses its capital because a capital is a thing masonry has and rock does not. `ragged_short_at` is the shortest a member may be as a fraction of the wall. Set `ragged: false` for masonry.
interior_structure._comment_corbel: A bracket under each end of every ceiling rib. The same critic's first finding was that the ribs 'simply penetrate the masonry -- nothing sags, nothing is broken, nothing carries a load'. A corbel is what a wall does to catch a beam; it also puts a second silhouette on the wall/ceiling line, which is the junction this whole pass is about. 0 removes them.

_comment_spawns: The warrens' own population, spawned through encounter_director.gd's `spawn_wild()` so these are ORDINARY wild creatures -- same engage prompt, same fight, same catching, same respawn. No second combat mode exists and none is wanted. `aggressive: true` overrides the species' own temperament for THESE bodies only (species.json still has Burrowback and Mudsnout as non-aggressive animals out in the meadow): a creature defending the tunnel it lives in comes at you, the same one grazing a field does not. `level` overrides the wild band roll (progression.json) -- the warrens is Band 2 content and its residents are above the field's. Ground species only, from the existing roster; no new species and no new meshes (Sec20, D23). Tuskroot is deliberately absent for the same reason spawns.json leaves it out: D20 makes it the EVOLVED form, obtainable only by evolving a caught Mudsnout.
_comment_spawns_sh47: SH47/D42 LEVELS LOWERED: mouth 10->9, hall 12->10, warren 11->10, den 13->11, and the guardian 18->14 below. Still TUNABLE, and the shape is unchanged -- the residents still climb as you go deeper and the guardian is still well above them. What moved is the STEP UP FROM BAND 1. Band 1's gate trainer (Oskar) fields levels 6 and 7 and spec Sec3 recommends a team of 5-8 at the bridge; arriving here at 7 to meet a 13 in the den and an 18 at the bottom was an eleven-level gulf, and tools/_probe_pacing.py measured what a player actually did about it: 25 wild fights against level-2-to-6 field creatures before daring to go in, 19 minutes of Sec11's `bad grind` bolted onto the front of the chapter's best dungeon. Clearing the warrens is on Sec11's GOOD list and nothing about it is cut -- the fights are the same fights, the deposits the same deposits, the heartstone still behind the guardian. They now sit where a player who played Band 1 actually is.
_comment_spawns_nickname: FIRST-HOUR-FUN-REBUILD. `nickname` is optional on any spawn entry and is used by exactly one of them. The vault encounter remains a named Elder Trailpup: a player who reaches the branch should understand this is an exceptional animal, not one more aggressive body in a dark room. The original Terrapup was removed because all three starter species are unique to Grandpa's opening choice and cannot be ordinary catchable wilds. Trailpup also deliberately differs from the Burrowback guardian, so the optional catch has its own quicker, higher-risk fight rather than reading as a second copy of the boss. The name is written the same two-object way the guardian's name is (burrow_warrens.gd::_spawn_population), so a caught one keeps its species underneath. Presentation only: level, temperament, catch rate and the fight are untouched.
_comment_spawns_special: BAND2-63 / FIRST-HOUR-FUN-REBUILD. Prompt 63 asks for 'at least one optional strong/rare encounter... worth seeing even if not caught', distinct from the required guardian fight. The Elder Trailpup is the warrens' established Ground species in an exceptional context: alone in the vault, past the Burrowback alpha and next to the heartstone. Level 13 sits one below the guardian's own 14 (still above the den's 11), so it reads as a real fight and not a formality, and it is entirely optional -- clear.flag already pays out when the guardian falls, so reaching this chamber is never a completion wall. It replaces the former wild Terrapup so the starter choice stays meaningful everywhere catchable wilds spawn.
_comment_guardian: Spec Sec3 Band 2 and Sec20: a STRONG NORMAL SPECIES, explicitly not a new legendary and explicitly not a new mesh. Burrowback is the roster's highest-defence Ground creature and the animal this whole warren belongs to, so the biggest one in it is the thing at the bottom. Level is well above its own residents and above the recommended Band 2 team, TUNABLE -- it is meant to be the fight you come back for, not a wall. It can be CAUGHT rather than beaten (catching is available during wild combat, CLAUDE.md; a guardian is not trainer-owned) and either way the warrens counts as cleared -- a dungeon that can only be resolved one of the two legal ways would be a rule this game does not have.
_comment_guardian_presentation: BAND2-63-WARRENS. Prompt 63's acceptance asks for a guardian that is "memorable, not standard fight + HP", and what shipped was a Burrowback at a higher number: the world prompt said `Engage Burrowback`, the combat plate said `Burrowback`, and the body was the same size as the three-metre-away residents. These two keys are presentation ONLY and deliberately so -- D23 forbids a new mesh and spec Sec20 forbids inventing a legendary, and CLAUDE.md names materials/modest scale/animation/VFX/encounter context as the differentiation that is allowed instead. `nickname` is written onto the spawned body's `display_name` (what `encounter_director.gd`'s engage prompt reads) AND the instance's `nickname` (what `creature_instance.label()` reads, so a player who CATCHES it keeps the name and the species underneath is not lost -- that is the bug encounter_director.gd:463 already documents). `art_scale` multiplies the model pivot, never the capsule: the collider, the hit cone's reach and the catch accuracy bonus are all built from species.json's `height`/`radius` on purpose (creature_body.gd::_build_placeholder), and scaling the fight instead of the silhouette would retune combat by changing a presentation number. TUNABLE.
_comment_guardian_alpha: CONTENT-0828, owner playtest 2026-08-28: 'there needs to be a point to going in the burrows warren. like a prize at the bottom or an alpha animal or something.' The cave already had both. What it did not have was a guardian that READS as an alpha -- and this game has a complete alpha system that the chapter's own boss was the only notable creature not using. `scale` replaces `art_scale`: the old key multiplied the model pivot ONLY, so the guardian had a three-metre silhouette over a field burrowback's capsule, hit cone and catch bonus (creature_body.gd's `body_scale` note calls that the invisible discrepancy PW2 forbids, and every band alpha in bands/*/spawns.json uses the multiplier instead). 1.4 -> 1.35 because it is now a real reach change and not just a picture. The alpha COLOURWAY, rim and mote aura cost nothing and were simply never switched on here: `creature_burrowback_lod0_base_color_alpha.png` -- CREATURE-IDENTITY-2's heavier-stone-plates repaint of this exact species -- has been installed all along. No new mesh and no invented legendary (D23, spec Sec20); material, texture, modest scale, VFX and encounter context are what CLAUDE.md names instead, and all of it already existed. ALL TUNABLE.
_comment_guardian_move: `signature_move` is a PER-INSTANCE override of the charged slot (creature_instance.gd holds move_quick/move_charged as plain fields), so ordinary burrowbacks out in the meadow keep species.json's `tremor_roll` and nothing about the species changes. This is what makes the fight a different fight rather than a longer one -- prompt 63's `memorable, not standard fight + HP`. `earth_fist` is 1.4x power against tremor_roll's 1.0 with a 0.62s windup and a 72-degree cone: heavier, telegraphed, and DIRECTIONAL, so a player who reads the windup can step around it. `earthshatter` is the stronger move and is deliberately NOT used -- 360 degrees at 7.5m inside a den whose combat_arena_bounds_at() clearance is about six metres cannot be stepped out of, and an unavoidable hit is not a memorable fight. A player who CATCHES the guardian keeps Earth Fist, which is the other half of why this is worth doing. Level stays 14: SH47/D42 lowered it against measured pacing and this pass does not reopen that.
_comment_clear: SB9's flat flag store (autoload/progression_state.gd), the same one trainer defeats, the road gate and the TM pickups already write to. `flag` is set the moment the guardian goes down; `reward` pays exactly once against it, so re-entering a cleared warrens is a walk through an empty cave, not a payout faucet. Reward shape is SC15's (`coins`/`items`/`xp_bonus`), on purpose -- the trainer payout is the same idea and a second reward format would drift from it.
_comment_clear_payout: CONTENT-0828 / FIRST-HOUR-FUN-REBUILD. The old payout was 45 coins, 4 rootstone and 60 xp, and chapter_rewards.json's own audit table is the argument against it: the chapter's ONE REQUIRED DUNGEON -- five resident fights, four deposits and a level-14 alpha, measured at 5-9 minutes -- paid less than Pell, the optional picket standing 35m outside its door (40 coins, 2 potions, 3 orbs), and a third of what relay_captain Vance pays one band later. A boss that pays picket money is a boss with no point, which is the owner's report in economic terms. This is the same reward SHAPE (SC15's coins/items/xp_bonus, no second system -- chapter_rewards.json's `_comment_no_new_systems` forbids one), at boss scale. The two Greater Orbs are deliberate: Pell pays BASIC orbs because the reward for clearing the door is the means to catch what is behind it. The guardian pays GREATER orbs because the door it opens leads to the level-13 Elder Trailpup beside the heartstone; the player can choose to catch it with a stronger tool, not a duplicate starter or second guardian. Beat the alpha, get the orbs, watch the door go down, and the optional encounter is standing next to the prize. ALL TUNABLE.

reward.message: The guardian goes down and the warren goes quiet. The slab across the deep branch grinds into the floor -- something is lit back there.

_why_t3_reward: T3-REWARD, owner-direction §14 ('Warrens Guardian: Rootstone progression + useful TM/equipment/recipe'). CONTENT-0828 already fixed the payout's SIZE (this row used to pay less than the optional picket standing outside the door); what it still lacked was the literal 'TM/equipment/recipe' item this row of the ladder asks for. Every Ground TM already has an acquisition path (world pickup or Mira's shop, and Field's own Sigil reward now adds a third), so a TM here would be one more copy of something obtainable elsewhere rather than a new reason to clear the dungeon. hide_vest is the largest of the five armor pieces in items.json (0.14 defence, GAME_DESIGN.md 18's trainer-armor slots) and, like the elixirs the three captains now hand out, had no acquisition path anywhere in the game before this -- the chapter's one required dungeon is exactly where 'found in the depths, past what was guarding it' reads as earned rather than bought.
_comment_deposits: Rootstone in the walls -- Sec3 Band 2's own material, the first tier above wood/stone/fiber/berries. These are harvest_node.gd nodes with their specs written HERE rather than in data/config/harvest.json: that file is the first day's tutorial gathering out in the meadow (and the Old Quarry lane owns its own additions to it), and a deposit inside a dungeon has no business being in the same list. `at` is chamber-local [x, z] like everything above.
_comment_deposit_models: BAND2-63-WARRENS round 2. These carried no `model`, and `harvest_node.gd` falls back to `_box_visual()` when a spec has none -- so every rootstone deposit in the cave rendered as an untextured pale placeholder cube. The blind critic found it twice without being told what it was looking at ('a bare placeholder box ... a placeholder block in a frame offered for judgement is a defect, twice'). Rocks from the same nature family the outcrop outside uses, at deposit scale: the seam the player breaks is now made of the stone the hill is made of.
_comment_dressing: BAND2-63-WARRENS. Prompt 63's required-dungeon list names `evidence of Team Tether activity` as part of the Burrow Warrens itself, and the band had none INSIDE the cave -- the only Team Tether trace in the region was the `quarry_supply_cache` prop cluster out at the ranger camp spur, which a player who walks the road to the warrens mouth and goes straight down never sees. This is that evidence, and it is deliberately EVIDENCE AND NOT EXPLANATION: the same rule `old_quarry.json`'s own `_comment_evidence` states for the quarry (Sec32's reveal ladder), so there is no note to read, no interactable, and nobody down here who knows what the seam is for. What the player is shown is a working face somebody was cutting rootstone out of and left mid-load, deeper in a cave than anyone local has a reason to be. Every model is from the ONE prop family the settlement already uses (`assets/props/quaternius_fantasy`, D24) and is the same crate/barrel/pickaxe vocabulary `quarry_station` puts on the quarry floor, so the player reads the two sites as one operation. Placed by `scripts/world/props.gd::place()` -- the same placer, collider and sink behaviour as every authored prop above ground -- through a `top_level` child so the cave's own `ground_height_at()` puts them on the CAVE FLOOR rather than on the hillside now several metres overhead. `chamber` + `offset` are chamber-local metres, the same authoring shape `spawns` above already uses, so the whole set rotates and translates with `site.at`/`site.yaw_deg` if this cave is ever relocated again. `yaw_deg` is likewise cave-local. NO ROPE: `Rope_1` is illegible at normal camera distance, a limitation the shipped `ranger_camp` cluster's own rope already has and this pass did not repeat.

dressing._why: the first thing inside the mouth, four paces in: one empty crate, so the very first read of the cave is somebody has been carrying things out of here, before a single creature or deposit is seen
the staging pile's anchor against the hall's east wall, well off both the mouth->den corridor at x=0 and the burrowback pair at [-4, 2] -- a load filled and never collected
set touching the first crate rather than merely near it, EV7-clusters-fix's own finding: a loose arc reads as dumped, a touching pile reads as one load
water for whoever was working the seam, kept with the load -- the detail that makes this a shift rather than a raid
leaning off vertical against the hall wall, the one prop that names the work -- and the same tool the rootstone deposits three metres away want from the player
somebody's pack, still here: the detail that makes the site abandoned rather than merely finished, exactly as it does at the quarry station

the deepest crate, a metre and a half from the den's own rootstone deposit and across the room from the guardian -- they got this far, they were still cutting, and then they stopped. This is what makes the animal at the bottom the reason the dig ended rather than a fight bolted onto the end of a corridor
tipped on its side beside that crate: the one prop in the cave that is not standing, so the den's pile reads as left in a hurry against the hall's, which reads as stacked
the edge of the deep pile, so the group has an edge instead of a boundary

BAND2-63-WARRENS round 2. The blind pass called the den bare -- 'one chest and one small scrap on an otherwise bare flat floor ... a den should show occupation'. This one is tipped and on the far side of the room from the rest, so the den reads as a place something large moves through rather than a store room
round 2: knocked well clear of the pile it belongs to, in the guardian's own half of the room
round 2: dropped deepest of all, past the guardian -- whoever carried it did not come back for it

_comment_prize_lead: BAND2-63-WARRENS. The pickup line carries the LEAD, not just the object. Prompt 63 asks this region to make the Mudsnout -> Tuskroot connection meaningful, and the lead was legible only to a player who happened to open the satchel and read the item description, or who owned a Mudsnout and pressed G on the creatures tab to be told `Mudsnout needs a Heartstone to evolve` (scripts/ui/tab_creatures.gd::_read_evolve, whose refusal string is where the requirement actually surfaces today). Both of those work and neither is guaranteed to happen in this region, which is where the stone is found. The line now says what the stone is FOR in the same words items.json already uses, at the one moment every player who takes it is looking at it. No rule changed: `progression.json`'s gate is still level 15 + bond 55 + heartstone, and this file does not touch it.
_comment_prize: R4.6 built the evolution item gate as real, unit-tested infrastructure and then left it switched OFF, because nothing in the world could source the item (see data/config/progression.json's own note). THIS is the source: the Heartstone, sitting in the one chamber that is off the critical path, behind the guardian. Taking it flips nothing by itself -- progression.json's `evolution.mudsnout.item_id` is what turns the gate on, and it is now `heartstone`. `flag` makes the pickup one-time across saves, the same rule tm_pickup.gd already keeps for a disc.

prize.label: Take the heartstone
prize.message: A heartstone. Warm, and beating slowly -- the kind of stone a creature is held against to finish becoming what it was already turning into.
